notation: Use SAME H, q and d>N from FIBERGROWTH. Let I=I_H on source L_infinity; q not in I. Omitted E_i have pole b_i, transverse r_i, residual delta_i and image equation c_i of degree D_i. S=sum b_i delta_i degD_i; lambda=d-S. N_H is the field norm identified back with the target rational-function field.
geometry: Every omitted E_i is centered in I, because H is regular and maps every point of L_infinity outside I to q at infinity. Every normalized live inverse valuation of nu_i is also centered in I: a valuation centered outside I maps to center q, and q is regular fixed, so cannot later map to I. Every forward image of every D_i has its only infinity q and degree d^j degD_i.
finite_norm_law: For irreducible f whose affine curve C has A1 normalization and H|C normalization degree1, finite normalization of the WHOLE A2 gives div N_H(f)=[H(C)]+sum_i delta_i ord_Ei(f)[D_i]. This is standard finite norm/divisor geometry, with no extra r_i. It is the old CURVE1758 calculation retained at named foundational tier; omitted orders may be negative and all coincident factors combine.
invariant_factor_group: For C with its only infinity q, ord_Ei f=-b_i deg f, while deg H(C)=d deg f. Hence N_H(f)=constant*f_H(C)/product c_i^(b_i delta_i deg f), and its ordinary degree at generic infinity is lambda deg f. The multiplicative group generated by such curve equations and constants is preserved by N_H, so ordinary degree at infinity is multiplied by lambda under every iterate, with cancellations harmless. No generic condition is chosen anew.
initial_generic_line: Choose one affine line ell=0 with infinity outside finite I. Then ord_Ei ell=-b_i, H(ell=0) has A1 normalization, degree d and only infinity q. N_H(ell) belongs to the preceding factor group and has degree at infinity lambda; therefore deg_infinity N_H^n(ell)=lambda^n. The same ell has ord_v ell=-b_v for every inverse v under consideration, since their centers are all in I.
inverse_pole_identity: For the finite degree-N^n field extension H^n, let H^n_*ord_v=e_v ord_Ei and f_v be the residue degree. Multiplicativity/transitivity of the norm and the finite DVR formula give ord_Ei N_(H^n)(ell)=sum_v f_v ord_v ell. All these v are at infinity and first reach E_i after n live steps; no earlier affine image can later return to infinity under a polynomial map. Since all norm factors have infinity q, the left side is -b_i lambda^n. Thus sum_v f_v b_v=b_i lambda^n. In particular lambda>0, and S>0 implies 0<lambda<d.
atom_lower_bounds: For each such v at depth n, choose a resolution of H^(n+1) retaining its divisor. Its complete divisor maps to D_i with residual degree f_v delta_i. Every subsequent iterate is regular near that divisor because D_i and its iterates have regular infinity q. The fixed-model/refinement argument yields mu({v})>=b_v f_v delta_i degD_i/d^(n+1). No common model for all v or all n, and no improper A7 is needed.
disjointness: First-exit generations and final E_i labels are disjoint. The statement is about finite atomic carriers for each generation, not that every Borel first-exit set has only finitely many elements; the preliminary blind proposal shorthand is corrected here.
probability_squeeze: If S>0, sum of all the displayed atom lower bounds is sum_(n>=0) [S/d]*(lambda/d)^n=1. Since mu is a probability, every lower bound is exact and the entire measure is supported on these countably many positive-discrepancy divisors. Thus mu(A=0)=0 in the hypothetical nonproper case. This conclusion follows from the atom squeeze and norm law without assuming the finite-moment balance or a one-sided lsc limit.
moment_check: Global Jac constant gives a_v=e_v r_i and A(v)=e_v r_i/b_v. The finite extension identity sum e_v f_v=N^n yields integral A dmu=sum_n W N^n/d^(n+1)=W/(d-N), matching the published moment theorem. No0*infinity or signed-functional continuity. If S=0, there are no omitted divisors and the existing moment/THIN result gives mu(A=0)=1 instead.
obstruction_to_original_test: The pole sum grows at lambda=d-S, not d. Thus if S>0, a uniform c*d^n lower bound contradicts the exact retained norm correction; it is not obtained from generic degree growth. The new candidate is a conditional full-measure renewal/dichotomy theorem, not W=0 or JC2.
remaining_gap: A countably atomic positive-discrepancy nef null eigenclass is not automatically Cartier/valuative. No generic rigidity, finite support, common finite model or zero positive-moment claim. The result would sharpen the counterexample structure, but still needs an actual global-J contradiction. No public promotion or source audit is claimed.
